}
for _name, _label in WIKI:
    _key = "wiki-" + _name[:-3]
    DOC_LINKS[_name] = (_key, _key)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Markdown -> HTML
def slugify(text, seen):
    """GitHub-style heading slug, made unique within one document."""
    s = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", text).strip().lower()
    s = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", s, flags=re.UNICODE).replace(" ", "-")
    base, n = s, 1
    while s in seen:
        s = f"{base}-{n}"
        n += 1
    seen.add(s)
    return s


def inline(text, prefix):
    """Inline Markdown: code spans, links, bold, italics. Everything else is escaped."""
    codes = []

    def keep_code(m):
        codes.append(m.group(1))
        return f"\x00{len(codes) - 1}\x00"

    text = re.sub(r"`([^`]+)`", keep_code, text)
    text = html.escape(text, quote=False)

    def link(m):
        label, url = m.group(1), m.group(2).strip()
        if url.startswith("#"):
            return f'<a href="#{prefix}-{url[1:]}">{label}</a>'
        if re.match(r"https?://", url):
            return f'<a href="{html.escape(url)}" target="_blank" rel="noopener">{label}</a>'
        # Links between this repository's documents point inside the compendium.
        target, _, anchor = url.partition("#")
        mapped = DOC_LINKS.get(os.path.basename(target))
        if mapped:
            anchor_prefix, section_id = mapped
            return f'<a href="#{anchor_prefix}-{anchor}">{label}</a>' if anchor else f'<a href="#{section_id}">{label}</a>'
        return f'<span class="file-ref" title="{html.escape(url)}">{label}</span>'

    text = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)\s]+)\)", link, text)
    text = re.sub(r"&lt;(https?://[^&\s]+)&gt;", r'<a href="\1" target="_blank" rel="noopener">\1</a>', text)
    text = re.sub(r"(?<![=\"'>/])(https?://[^\s<)\]]+[^\s<)\].,;:])", r'<a href="\1" target="_blank" rel="noopener">\1</a>', text)
    text = re.sub(r"\*\*(.+?)\*\*", r"<strong>\1</strong>", text)
    text = re.sub(r"(?<![\w*])\*(?!\s)(.+?)(?<!\s)\*(?![\w*])", r"<em>\1</em>", text)
    return re.sub(r"\x00(\d+)\x00", lambda m: f"<code>{html.escape(codes[int(m.group(1))], quote=False)}</code>", text)


def split_row(line):
    cells = re.split(r"(?<!\\)\|", line.strip().strip("|"))
    return [c.strip().replace("\\|", "|") for c in cells]


LIST_RE = re.compile(r"^(\s*)([-*+]|\d+[.)])\s+(.*)$")


def md_to_html(md, prefix, drop_title=True):
    lines = md.replace("\r\n", "\n").split("\n")
    out, seen, i, first_h1 = [], set(), 0, drop_title

    def flush_para(buf):
        if buf:
            out.append(f"<p>{inline(' '.join(x.strip() for x in buf), prefix)}</p>")
            buf.clear()

    para = []
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        if line.strip().startswith("```"):
            flush_para(para)
            lang = line.strip()[3:].strip()
            body = []
            i += 1
            while i < len(lines) and not lines[i].strip().startswith("```"):
                body.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            i += 1
            cls = f' class="lang-{html.escape(lang)}"' if lang else ""
            out.append(f"<pre><code{cls}>{html.escape(chr(10).join(body), quote=False)}</code></pre>")
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*$", line)
        if m:
            flush_para(para)
            level, text = len(m.group(1)), m.group(2)
            if level == 1 and first_h1:
                first_h1 = False
                i += 1
                continue
            tag = f"h{min(6, max(3, level + 1))}"
            out.append(f'<{tag} id="{prefix}-{slugify(text, seen)}">{inline(text, prefix)}</{tag}>')
            i += 1
            continue
        if re.match(r"^\s*(---+|\*\*\*+)\s*$", line):
            flush_para(para)
            out.append("<hr>")
            i += 1
            continue
        if line.lstrip().startswith("|") and i + 1 < len(lines) and re.match(r"^\s*\|?\s*:?-{2,}", lines[i + 1]):
            flush_para(para)
            head = split_row(line)
            i += 2
            rows = []
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].lstrip().startswith("|"):
                rows.append(split_row(lines[i]))
                i += 1
            t = ['<div class="tw"><table><thead><tr>' + "".join(f"<th>{inline(c, prefix)}</th>" for c in head) + "</tr></thead><tbody>"]
            for r in rows:
                t.append("<tr>" + "".join(f"<td>{inline(c, prefix)}</td>" for c in r) + "</tr>")
            t.append("</tbody></table></div>")
            out.append("".join(t))
            continue
        if line.startswith(">"):
            flush_para(para)
            quote = []
            while i < len(lines) and lines[i].startswith(">"):
                quote.append(lines[i][1:].lstrip() if lines[i][1:2] == " " else lines[i][1:])
                i += 1
            out.append(f"<blockquote>{md_to_html(chr(10).join(quote), prefix, drop_title=False)}</blockquote>")
            continue
        if LIST_RE.match(line):
            flush_para(para)
            items = []  # (indent, ordered, text)
            while i < len(lines):
                lm = LIST_RE.match(lines[i])
                if lm:
                    items.append([len(lm.group(1).expandtabs(4)), lm.group(2)[0].isdigit(), lm.group(3)])
                    i += 1
                elif lines[i].strip() and lines[i].startswith((" ", "\t")) and items and not lines[i].strip().startswith("```"):
                    items[-1][2] += " " + lines[i].strip()
                    i += 1
                else:
                    break
            out.append(render_list(items, prefix))
            continue
        if not line.strip():
            flush_para(para)
            i += 1
            continue
        para.append(line)
        i += 1
    flush_para(para)
    return "\n".join(out)


def render_list(items, prefix):
    html_parts, stack = [], []  # stack of (indent, tag)
    for indent, ordered, text in items:
        tag = "ol" if ordered else "ul"
        while stack and indent < stack[-1][0]:
            html_parts.append(f"</li></{stack.pop()[1]}>")
        if not stack or indent > stack[-1][0]:
            html_parts.append(f"<{tag}>")
            stack.append((indent, tag))
        else:
            html_parts.append("</li>")
        html_parts.append(f"<li>{inline(text, prefix)}")
    while stack:
        html_parts.append(f"</li></{stack.pop()[1]}>")
    return "".join(html_parts)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the teaching page
PAGE = read("site/orchestrating-claude.html")
# The page shows its own version in its footer; read it there, never hard-code it.
PAGE_VERSION, PAGE_UPDATED = re.search(r"Version (\d+), last updated (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\.", PAGE).groups()


def page_document(src):
    # No web fonts inside the compendium: the page falls back to system fonts, so nothing loads over the network.
    src = re.sub(r'<link rel="(?:preconnect|stylesheet)" href="https://fonts\.[^"]+"[^>]*>\n?', "", src)
    return '<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"></head><body>' + src + "</body></html>"


def page_text_blocks(src):
    """The page's lessons as plain text, one block per paragraph, for reading and search."""
    blocks = []
    for m in re.finditer(r'<section id="([^"]+)"[^>]*>(.*?)</section>', src, re.S):
        sid, body = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        body = re.sub(r"<(script|style)\b.*?</\1>", " ", body, flags=re.S)
        body = re.sub(r'<p class="lesson-end">.*?</p>', " ", body, flags=re.S)
        kicker = re.search(r'<p class="kicker">(.*?)</p>', body, re.S)
        title = re.search(r"<h2>(.*?)</h2>", body, re.S)
        clean = lambda s: html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", s)).split()
        head = " ".join(clean(kicker.group(1))) if kicker else sid
        head = re.sub(r"\s*(Core|Builder|Reference) · \d+ min$", "", head)
        h2 = " ".join(clean(title.group(1))) if title else ""
        body = re.sub(r"<(/?)(p|li|h3|h4|tr|figcaption|summary|dt|dd|div|text|pre)\b[^>]*>", "\n", body)
        paras = [" ".join(clean(p)) for p in body.split("\n")]
        paras = [p for p in paras if len(p) > 1 and p not in (h2,)]
        blocks.append((sid, head, h2, paras))
    return blocks


def page_sources(src):
    """The page's Sources lesson as (group, title, url, grade) rows."""
    a = src.index('<section id="sources"')
    b = src.index("</section>", a)
    rows, group = [], ""
    for m in re.finditer(r'<h3>(.*?)</h3>|<li><a href="([^"]+)"[^>]*>(.*?)</a>\s*<a class="ev ([psrd])"', src[a:b], re.S):
        if m.group(1):
            group = html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", m.group(1)))
        else:
            rows.append((group, html.unescape(m.group(3)), html.unescape(m.group(2)), m.group(4).upper()))
    return rows


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- sections
GRADE = {"P": "Primary", "S": "Second-hand", "R": "Research", "D": "Design advice"}


def code_listing(rel, note):
    src = read(rel)
    lines = src.count("\n") + 1
    return (f'<details class="code"><summary><code>{html.escape(rel)}</code> <span class="muted">· {lines} lines · {html.escape(note)}</span></summary>'
            f'<pre><code>{html.escape(src, quote=False)}</code></pre></details>')


def doc(rel, prefix, label=None):
    body = md_to_html(read(rel), prefix)
    src = f'<p class="src-path">Source: <code>{html.escape(rel)}</code></p>'
    if label:
        return f'<section class="sub" id="{prefix}"><h3 class="subhead">{html.escape(label)}</h3>{src}{body}</section>'
    return src + body

section("reproduce", "Reproduce and verify", "How the checks work, their results, and the scripts.", repro)
section("agents", "Working on this repository", "The agent instructions that ship with the repository.", doc("AGENTS.md", "agents"))

    for i, (sid, t, lead, body) in enumerate(sections))

JS = r"""
(function(){
  /* ---------- theme: system, light or dark; remembered when storage is available ---------- */
  var root = document.documentElement, themeBtn = document.getElementById('theme');
  var modes = ['system', 'light', 'dark'];
  function applyTheme(m){
    if(m === 'system') root.removeAttribute('data-theme'); else root.setAttribute('data-theme', m);
    themeBtn.textContent = 'Theme: ' + m;
  }
  var mode = 'system';
  try { mode = localStorage.getItem('compendium-theme') || 'system'; } catch(e) {}
  applyTheme(mode);
  themeBtn.addEventListener('click', function(){
    mode = modes[(modes.indexOf(mode) + 1) % modes.length];
    applyTheme(mode);
    try { localStorage.setItem('compendium-theme', mode); } catch(e) {}
  });

  /* ---------- contents rail: mark the section in view ---------- */
  var tocLinks = document.querySelectorAll('.toc a');
  var secs = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('main .sec'));
  function markToc(){
    var line = window.innerHeight * 0.25, cur = secs[0];
    secs.forEach(function(s){ if(s.getBoundingClientRect().top <= line) cur = s; });
    tocLinks.forEach(function(a){
      var on = a.getAttribute('href') === '#' + cur.id;
      a.classList.toggle('on', on);
      if(on) a.setAttribute('aria-current', 'location'); else a.removeAttribute('aria-current');
    });
  }
  window.addEventListener('scroll', markToc, {passive: true});
  markToc();

  /* ---------- open whatever hides an element, then show it ---------- */
  function reveal(el){
    for(var p = el.parentElement; p; p = p.parentElement){ if(p.tagName === 'DETAILS') p.open = true; }
  }
  function show(el){
    reveal(el);
    el.scrollIntoView({block: 'center'});
    el.classList.remove('flash'); void el.offsetWidth; el.classList.add('flash');
  }
  document.addEventListener('click', function(e){
    var a = e.target.closest('a[href^="#"]');
    if(!a || a.getAttribute('href').length < 2) return;
    var t = document.getElementById(a.getAttribute('href').slice(1));
    if(t) reveal(t);
  });

  /* ---------- search: every paragraph, list item, table row and code block ---------- */
  var SEL = 'h3,h4,h5,p,li,tr,pre,summary,blockquote';
  var index = [];
  document.querySelectorAll('main .sec').forEach(function(sec){
    var title = sec.getAttribute('data-title');
    sec.querySelectorAll(SEL).forEach(function(el){
      if(el.querySelector(SEL)) return;
      var raw = el.tagName === 'TR' ? Array.prototype.map.call(el.cells, function(c){ return c.textContent; }).join(' · ') : el.textContent;
      var text = raw.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
      if(text.length > 1) index.push({el: el, text: text, low: text.toLowerCase(), sec: title});
    });
  });
  document.getElementById('stat-blocks').textContent = index.length.toLocaleString();

  var input = document.getElementById('q'), list = document.getElementById('results'), count = document.getElementById('q-count');
  var hits = [], sel = -1, marked = [];
  function esc(s){ return s.replace(/[&<>"]/g, function(c){ return {'&':'&amp;','<':'&lt;','>':'&gt;','"':'&quot;'}[c]; }); }
  function snippet(text, terms){
    var low = text.toLowerCase(), at = low.indexOf(terms[0]);
    var start = Math.max(0, at - 60), part = text.slice(start, start + 200);
    var out = esc(part);
    terms.forEach(function(t){
      if(!t) return;
      out = out.replace(new RegExp('(' + t.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&') + ')', 'ig'), '<mark>$1</mark>');
    });
    return (start > 0 ? '… ' : '') + out + (start + 200 < text.length ? ' …' : '');
  }
  function clearMarks(){
    marked.forEach(function(m){ var p = m.parentNode; if(!p) return; p.replaceChild(document.createTextNode(m.textContent), m); p.normalize(); });
    marked = [];
  }
  function markIn(el, terms){
    var walker = document.createTreeWalker(el, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT), nodes = [], n;
    while((n = walker.nextNode())) nodes.push(n);
    var re = new RegExp('(' + terms.map(function(t){ return t.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&'); }).join('|') + ')', 'ig');
    nodes.forEach(function(node){
      if(!re.test(node.nodeValue)) return;
      re.lastIndex = 0;
      var frag = document.createDocumentFragment(), last = 0, m;
      node.nodeValue.replace(re, function(match, g, off){
        frag.appendChild(document.createTextNode(node.nodeValue.slice(last, off)));
        var mk = document.createElement('mark'); mk.textContent = match; frag.appendChild(mk); marked.push(mk);
        last = off + match.length;
        return match;
      });
      frag.appendChild(document.createTextNode(node.nodeValue.slice(last)));
      node.parentNode.replaceChild(frag, node);
    });
  }
  function render(){
    list.innerHTML = '';
    if(!input.value.trim()){ list.hidden = true; count.textContent = ''; return; }
    if(!hits.length){ list.innerHTML = '<li class="r-none">No matches. Try fewer or shorter words.</li>'; list.hidden = false; count.textContent = '0'; return; }
    var terms = input.value.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
    hits.slice(0, 80).forEach(function(h, i){
      var li = document.createElement('li');
      li.innerHTML = '<button type="button" role="option" id="r' + i + '" aria-selected="' + (i === sel) + '"><span class="r-sec">' + esc(h.sec) + '</span>' + snippet(h.text, terms) + '</button>';
      li.firstChild.addEventListener('click', function(){ go(i); });
      list.appendChild(li);
    });
    count.textContent = hits.length > 80 ? '80 of ' + hits.length : String(hits.length);
    list.hidden = false;
  }
  function run(){
    var terms = input.value.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
    hits = terms.length ? index.filter(function(b){ return terms.every(function(t){ return b.low.indexOf(t) >= 0; }); }) : [];
    sel = hits.length ? 0 : -1;
    render();
  }
  function go(i){
    var h = hits[i]; if(!h) return;
    clearMarks();
    markIn(h.el, input.value.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean));
    list.hidden = true;
    show(h.el);
  }
  input.addEventListener('input', run);
  input.addEventListener('focus', function(){ if(input.value.trim()) render(); });
  input.addEventListener('keydown', function(e){
    if(e.key === 'ArrowDown' || e.key === 'ArrowUp'){
      e.preventDefault();
      var max = Math.min(hits.length, 80) - 1; if(max < 0) return;
      sel = e.key === 'ArrowDown' ? Math.min(max, sel + 1) : Math.max(0, sel - 1);
      render();
      var b = document.getElementById('r' + sel); if(b) b.scrollIntoView({block: 'nearest'});
    } else if(e.key === 'Enter'){ e.preventDefault(); go(Math.max(0, sel)); }
    else if(e.key === 'Escape'){ input.value = ''; clearMarks(); run(); }
  });
  input.setAttribute('aria-controls', 'results');
  document.addEventListener('keydown', function(e){
    if(e.key === '/' && document.activeElement !== input && !/INPUT|TEXTAREA|SELECT/.test(document.activeElement.tagName)){ e.preventDefault(); input.focus(); input.select(); }
  });
  document.addEventListener('click', function(e){ if(!e.target.closest('.search')) list.hidden = true; });

  /* ---------- the embedded page, on its own ---------- */
  var openPage = document.getElementById('open-page');
  if(openPage){
    openPage.addEventListener('click', function(){
      var frame = document.querySelector('.page-frame');
      var url = URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([frame.getAttribute('srcdoc')], {type: 'text/html'}));
      var w = window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener');
      if(!w) location.href = url;
    });
  }

  /* ---------- print everything, not only the open parts ---------- */
  window.addEventListener('beforeprint', function(){ document.querySelectorAll('details').forEach(function(d){ d.open = true; }); });
})();
"""

words = len(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", main).split())

    17

    Working on this repository

    The agent instructions that ship with the repository.

    Source: AGENTS.md

    Instructions for any agent working in this repository: Claude Code, Codex, or another tool.

    What this repository is

    A guide for building, orchestrating and guiding AI coding agents. It has four layers, and each has one source of truth:

    1. playbook/agent-harness-playbook.md is the canonical reference. Facts, laws, patterns and Templates A to M live here, each graded P (primary), S (second-hand), R (research) or D (design advice).
    2. wiki/ holds short runbooks distilled from the playbook. A wiki page links to the playbook section it summarises and adds no facts of its own.
    3. site/orchestrating-claude.html is the teaching page, published as a claude.ai artifact. It teaches the same material in 17 lessons.
    4. site/index.html, docs/orchestrating-claude-compendium.html, guide-index.json, routes/ and sections/ are generated. Never edit them by hand; rebuild them.

    When the playbook and another layer disagree, the playbook wins. Fix the other layer and say so in the commit.

    Finding your way

    • A session in another project starts at ENTRY.md. Read playbook sections with python3 -I tools/section.py <id> (for example 9.5, F or law-7; --list shows every id), never the whole playbook. Read cannot follow #anchors, and the playbook is about 1,500 lines.
    • orchestration-index.md is the phase index. Find the phase you are in, then read only the playbook sections it lists. Do not load the whole playbook when one phase's sections will do.
    • llms.txt maps every important file with a one-line description.
    • Every folder has a README.md that lists its files.
    • To answer a question from the playbook, go through its Contents or Find-it-fast table, then read that section.

    Using this repository as guidance

    When someone asks you to plan, run or review agent work, use this repository's own method:

    • Before a task: follow wiki/start-a-task.md. Grill first for anything above trivial (wiki/grill.md), then write a goal with Template B and an issue with Template L.
    • Splitting work: follow wiki/orchestrate.md. One writer by default; helpers read, search or review; brief them with Template C.
    • Proving work: follow wiki/verify.md. Every claim of done carries a receipt: each check marked PASS, FAIL or NOT RUN, with its command. NOT RUN is not PASS.
    • Unattended runs: follow wiki/run-unattended.md and wiki/guardrails.md. Every loop has a stop condition, a retry cap and a cost ceiling.
    • A stuck agent: follow wiki/unstick.md. It covers looping, a false "done", the same mistake twice, lost context and overbuilding.

    Editing rules

    Privacy (hard rule)

    • This repository is public. Never commit client or employer names, personal paths, email addresses, session ids or personal harness details.
    • Use repo-relative paths or a placeholder such as /path/to/claude-guides. Describe a private setup in general terms.
    • To add terms of your own to the check, list them one per line in .privacy-terms. That file is git-ignored and stays on your machine.
    • The repository's own public addresses (owner/repo, the Pages host) are listed in the committed .privacy-public. A private term inside one of them passes; anywhere else it still fails. Add only full addresses there, never a bare name.
    • Run python3 -I tools/check_privacy.py before every commit. It must PASS.

    Facts

    • Add no new factual claim without a primary source. Run a fact check, such as the doc-checker agent, before a claim lands.
    • Keep the evidence grade on every claim.
    • Keep the source list in sync: on the page, every evidence-tag URL must stay (checks/urls-v11.txt is the floor); new URLs are allowed.

    The page (site/orchestrating-claude.html)

    • One writer at a time. Parallel agents write drafts to issues/drafts/ and the lead splices them in. tools/splice_figs.py handles figures.
    • Follow the artifact contract:
      • no doctype, html or body tags
      • colours only as tokens on :root, with dark values under prefers-color-scheme and [data-theme]
      • external links open in a new tab
      • scripts only from the CDN allowlist
    • Keep the section ids (#loop … #sources) and the lesson numbers. The playbook map and old links depend on them.
    • Follow the visual language in the page's CSS comment above the diagram classes:
      • you: an accent pill
      • Claude: a neutral box
      • automatic, or the next run: dashed
      • pass: green
      • sent back: orange, and nothing else
      • harm, or a worse result: red
    • Draw figures at most 880 units wide, never scaled below 1:1, with text of 12px or more.
    • Glossary terms (a.term, #glossary [data-term]) must be defined in the block where they first appear. Check dom-9 enforces this.
    • After editing text, run python3 -I tools/lesson_meta.py site/orchestrating-claude.html to refresh reading times.
    • After any edit, run python3 -I tools/build_standalone.py to refresh site/index.html, the copy people open locally. checks/static.sh fails while it is stale. Never edit site/index.html by hand.

    Wiki, playbook and index

    • Link playbook sections by their GitHub anchor. After editing any heading or link, run python3 -I tools/check_links.py; every line should read PASS.
    • After editing the playbook, the cheat sheet, ENTRY.md, a runbook title or a skill's frontmatter, run python3 -I tools/build_index.py. It regenerates guide-index.json, routes/ and sections/, which agents without a clone fetch. Never edit them by hand.
    • When you add or rename a playbook section, run python3 -I tools/check_entry.py. ENTRY.md routes by section id, so a renamed or removed section breaks its router.
    • When you add a file, add it to its folder's README and, if it matters to agents, to llms.txt.
    • Write short, active, plain sentences: no marketing tone, no em-dash asides.

    Checks: what "done" means here

    The whole offline suite is one command. Run it before every commit; it must end with SUMMARY all PASS:

    tests/run.sh

    It runs every check below and every test in tests/, in under 10 seconds. tests/README.md explains what each test guards and how to run the mutation, live and browser layers. When you change a test, a check or a guarded file, also run python3 -I tests/mutation/mutate.py; every mutation must be CAUGHT. A guard that fails on purpose (a section renamed by design, say) is updated in the same commit, as tests/README.md describes. Never weaken or delete a test to make it pass.

    The individual checks, for when one fails. Run the privacy check before every commit:

    python3 -I tools/check_privacy.py

    Every line should read PASS. It fails on personal paths, email addresses, session ids and any term in .privacy-terms.

    checks/static.sh

    Every line should read PASS. The script also writes build/preview.html.

    Then run checks/run-dom.js with Playwright (browser_run_code_unsafe, filename set to that file; set ROOT in it to your clone). All checks should read PASS in all 8 views: 320, 375, 414, 768, 1024 and 1280px, in light and dark.

    Then check the links and the entry point, and rebuild the compendium:

    python3 -I tools/check_links.py
    python3 -I tools/check_entry.py

    check_entry.py confirms ENTRY.md is under 150 lines, has at least 15 router rows, and names only section ids that tools/section.py resolves.

    python3 -I tools/build_compendium.py

    The compendium check (checks/compendium-check.js) confirms the result has no network requests, no dangling links and no sideways scroll.

    Report results as receipts: <path:line-range> — <change> | verified: PASS <command>, or FAIL, or NOT RUN with the reason.

    Get an independent review for any change to facts, figures or interaction. Give the reviewer the files and the brief, never your conclusions.

    Publishing the page

    The live page is https://claude.ai/artifact/8q1jNZyZ1HTjDBvqgBWMLq. Publish updates to that same URL with the Artifact tool, passing url. Publishing is outward-facing, so do it only when the owner asks.

    Every push to main also publishes site/index.html (as the site's home page), the compendium (as compendium.html), and llms.txt, guide-index.json and every tracked Markdown file outside tests/live/ at its repository path, to GitHub Pages, through .github/workflows/pages.yml. Merging to main therefore publishes; rebuild both files before you merge.

    Git

    • Work on a branch, not on main.
    • Each clone runs git config merge.ours.driver true once: .gitattributes marks the generated compendium merge=ours, so a merge or revert keeps it, and you rebuild it after. How main was formed: docs/main-branch.md.
    • Make small, logical commits with plain messages.
    • Add no AI attribution: no Co-Authored-By trailer and no "Generated with" line.
    • Never commit secrets, .env files or build/.
